questions: What travels from the Sun to the leaf?
What two things does the plant take in, and what two things does it produce?
segments.say: Plants make their own food. Watch the light energy stream from the Sun into the leaf: green plants make glucose using that light energy, taking in carbon dioxide and water and releasing oxygen. Tell your partner: what are the inputs, and what are the products?

questions: By what route does each raw material reach the leaf?
What would happen to photosynthesis if the roots could not supply water?
segments.say: In: carbon dioxide and water. Follow the carbon dioxide as it flows into the leaf through tiny pores on its underside, then follow the water climbing from the roots. Both raw materials have to arrive at the leaf before any food can be built.

questions: Which product stays as the plant food, and which leaves the plant?
Where in the leaf does the building happen?
segments.say: Out: glucose and oxygen. With chlorophyll trapping the light, the plant builds glucose - that is the food - and the oxygen drifts out of the leaf into the air as a by-product. Say the word equation with me: carbon dioxide + water -> glucose + oxygen.

questions: What would happen to almost all life if photosynthesis stopped?
segments.say: Energy in, food out. Light energy powers the whole change, and the glucose made here feeds not just the plant but, through food chains, almost all life on Earth. That is why plants are called producers. Point at the scene and trace the energy: Sun, leaf, glucose.

questions: Where does the released oxygen actually come from?
What job does the carbon dioxide do instead?
segments.say: Here is the trap, sprung on purpose: it is tempting to think the oxygen comes from the carbon dioxide, because one goes in as the other comes out. Watch the wrong arrow vanish and the right arrow appear: the oxygen comes from water. Now work through the worksheet in pairs, checking each answer against the trap section of your student notes. Last, the exit ticket - on your own, no talking - and remember: if you can say where the oxygen really comes from, you have cracked today's lesson.
segments.watchFor: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from carbon dioxide. Listen for students who say exactly this when they explain the products. Send them back to the split water: the oxygen is released from water, while carbon dioxide supplies the carbon for glucose.
